incident: Shai-Hulud: Here We Go Again npm/PyPI supply-chain compromise

scope.scannerPackageSet: JFrog Here We Go Again package/version indicators plus selected confirmed broader Mini Shai-Hulud npm, PyPI, and Composer package/version indicators
scope.officialTanStackScope: 42 packages, 84 malicious versions, published on 2026-05-11 between 19:20 and 19:26 UTC
scope.campaignContext: JFrog reports more than 170 npm packages and 2 PyPI packages affected as of 2026-05-12. Socket reports 416 affected package artifacts for the broader Mini Shai-Hulud campaign as of 2026-05-12, spanning npm, PyPI, and one Composer artifact. Socket reports an active May 19 @antv npm publish wave tied to Mini Shai-Hulud and the npm maintainer account atool. Socket's technical analysis describes install-time index.js payloads, direct C2 at t.m-kosche.com, GitHub fallback exfiltration with reversed Shai-Hulud markers, and worm-like npm propagation using stolen npm tokens. May 22-23 ClickFix reporting and operator-provided VirusTotal context described compromised legitimate websites loading a remote script from staticcloudflare[.]pro with a reversed loader marker. Aikido's May 27 report describes codexui-android npm builds from 0.1.82 onward exfiltrating OpenAI Codex auth.json data to sentry.anyclaw[.]store/startlog. Calif's June 2026 HTTP/2 Bomb research and The Register coverage describe an Apache HTTP Server DoS tracked as CVE-2026-49975 and fixed in mod_http2 v2.0.41 by counting merged cookie headers against LimitRequestFields; this scanner flags copied incident notes and Apache config/version evidence for that fixed floor. Aikido, OX, and JFrog Red Hat / Miasma reporting describes compromised @redhat-cloud-services npm packages published via GitHub Actions OIDC/trusted publishing abuse, with a credential-stealing Mini Shai-Hulud variant calling itself Miasma, decoy api.anthropic.com/v1/api traffic, staged GitHub payload retrieval from letsgo0/sayyadina-phibian-159, OX's June 4 Miasma return report naming 57 affected npm packages plus a later edited weaponized binding.gyp wave adding discord-search, create-cf-token, @forjacms packages, dbmux, creditcard.js, github-archiver, and @contaazul/n8n-nodes-contaazul and the Miasma – The Spreading Blight marker, and JFrog/OX June 4 binding.gyp reporting describing evasive node-gyp command expansion through <!(...) as an alternate install-time execution path. OX's June 4 Malware-Slop 2 report describes cms-store-ren as an all-version malicious npm infostealer using Telegram Bot API exfiltration and hidden PowerShell execution. GitHub Advisory GHSA-g6v5-9xpp-6hpx and supplychainattack.org describe google-cloud-secret-manager-config-poc as all-version npm malware requiring full-compromise handling if installed or run. GitHub Advisory GHSA-6vr2-5hpq-589c and supplychainattack.org describe node-core-libs as npm malware requiring full-compromise handling if installed or run. GitHub Advisories GHSA-qp73-r9hh-6vq9 and GHSA-8j4q-hx83-pfq9 plus supplychainattack.org describe ts-grok and signup-embedder as npm malware with affected versions >= 0 and no patched versions, requiring full-compromise handling if installed or run. Panther's April 2026 OtterCookie npm report describes exact malicious wrapper/payload package versions, Vercel-hosted C2 infrastructure, postinstall execution, file exfiltration, and SSH authorized_keys backdoor behavior. DFIR Radar's June 25 note on malicious JetBrains plugins adds implementation details to the Aikido/BleepingComputer JetBrains AI-key stealer lane: save/apply configuration persistence exfiltration, BaseUtil.request(), sk- key validation, static auth token F48D2AA7CF341F782C1D, and plaintext HTTP POST from JetBrains processes. Flatt Security's June 1 Claude Code GitHub Action research describes a GitHub App actor bypass in agent mode, risky allowed_non_write_users configurations, OIDC token exfiltration through ACTIONS_ID_TOKEN_REQUEST_TOKEN / ACTIONS_ID_TOKEN_REQUEST_URL, and GitHub issue update exfiltration via MCP tools; Anthropic fixed the bypass as of Claude Code GitHub Actions v1.0.94. Lupin & Holmes' May 14 node-ipc reporting describes malicious node-ipc 9.1.6, 9.2.3, and 12.0.1 publishes by the dormant atiertant maintainer identity, likely email takeover through the re-registered atlantis-software.net domain, DNS-tunneling exfiltration, and C2 at sh.azurestaticprovider.net. A June 3 operator-provided package table added exact @ccrm and @emcd-vue npm package/version indicators for the Moika follow-up cluster. JFrog's June 3 IronWorm report describes compromised asteroiddao/WeaveDB npm package publishes using a preinstall hook that runs ./tools/setup, a Rust-built Linux infostealer with eBPF rootkit behavior, and forged/backdated GitHub commits attributed to claude-like automation identities. Windows 11 KB5094126 is tracked only as adjacent patch-regression awareness for BitLocker/HP/EFI rollback planning, not as a scanner indicator. Exact scanner detections are stored in this file; namespace and package-name warnings remain lower-confidence review prompts until exact malicious versions are confirmed. OX Security reported the June 17, 2026 easy-day-js / Mastra npm supply-chain attack affecting 141 packages through a malicious dayjs dependency swap, postinstall setup.cjs execution, and crypto-stealer C2 indicators. Socket later published stage-2 easy-day-js / Mastra details, including protocal.cjs, nvmconf.service, NodePackages persistence, Hostwinds C2 hostnames, /update/49890878, wallet-extension inventory behavior, browser-history collection, and SHA-256 hashes. SafeDep reported a June 16, 2026 procwire / routecraft npm campaign in which five coordinated packages split a Windows-only preinstall dropper across procwire, routecraft, endpointmap, bytecraft, and staticlayer, reconstructing a catbox.moe payload URL, using Microsoft-Delivery-Optimization/10.0, curl.exe, bitsadmin, hidden process execution, and Mark-of-the-Web stripping. JFrog reported hijacked html-to-gutenberg@4.2.11 and fetch-page-assets@1.2.9 npm packages using VS Code folder-open tasks, a fake fa-solid-400.woff2 JavaScript payload, blockchain dead drops, socket.io backdoor behavior, and Python infostealer staging; Nextron reported related Go-package reuse of the same fake-font payload hashes as OSINT follow-up. JFrog's June 25, 2026 Shai-Hulud/Hades analysis adds affected @immobiliarelabs/backstage-plugin-gitlab and ldap-auth package versions plus SEED_PAT/Seeder operator-seeding markers to the Leo/RStreams Miasma/Hades npm lane. SafeDep's June 25 LeoPlatform follow-up confirms 20 compromised LeoPlatform npm package versions and adds repository poisoning details around orphan snapshot-* branches, fake Dependabot Updates workflows, _index.js execution, OIDC_PACKAGES, WORKFLOW_ID, REPO_ID_SUFFIX, and NPM_TOKEN publication surfaces.
